items.name: UN language examinations
items.what: The main route into UN translator posts. Exams open for specific languages at certain times.
items.tip: Read who can apply, then check the announcements below for an Arabic or French exam.

items.name: UN examination announcements
items.what: Where the UN announces new language exams and its Global Language Register.
items.tip: Check this once a month. Exams can close within a few weeks.

items.name: UN Careers: language jobs
items.what: UN Careers' page for language professionals.
items.tip: Create your UN Careers profile now, so applying later only takes a few minutes.

items.name: WIPO consultant contracts
items.what: WIPO lists individual consultant contracts here, sometimes including language work.
items.tip: Look for translation, terminology or language titles.

items.name: UN Volunteers online
items.what: Online volunteering for UN agencies and partners.
items.tip: Search for translation tasks. Volunteering can give you UN references.

items.name: CLEAR Global (Translators without Borders)
items.what: Volunteer translation community for humanitarian organizations.
items.tip: Good humanitarian experience to list on a UN-style CV.

items.name: Tarjimly
items.what: Language services organization focused on humanitarian work.
items.tip: Check the site for how translators can join.

items.name: Lionbridge freelance community
items.what: Large translation company that hires freelancers through its community.
items.tip: Have your CV, language pairs and rates ready before you sign up.

items.name: TransPerfect
items.what: Large translation company. Its careers page covers freelance linguists.
items.tip: Look for the freelance linguist section and apply with your language pairs.

items.name: Acolad freelance opportunities
items.what: European translation group with a freelance network.
items.tip: Choose Freelance Opportunities on the page.

items.name: LanguageLine freelance translators
items.what: Translation and interpreting company with a freelance translator page.
items.tip: Check which languages and countries it accepts before applying.

items.name: Future Group
items.what: Translation and localization company that has posted Egypt jobs in your results.
items.tip: Check its open roles and follow the company for new ones.

items.name: Smartcat Marketplace
items.what: Translation marketplace where clients find freelance translators.
items.tip: A complete profile with your pairs and subject areas gets more requests.

items.name: Gengo
items.what: Online translation platform that accepts translators after a test.
items.tip: Take the test when you're rested. You can usually only try a limited number of times.

items.name: Translated
items.what: Translation company with a page for translators who want to work with it.
items.tip: Apply with your strongest language pair first.

items.name: ProZ.com profile
items.what: The largest community of professional translators. Clients search profiles there.
items.tip: Fill in your profile fully, including your language pairs and UN experience.

items.name: Wuzzuf job alerts
items.what: Egypt's job site. It blocks this tool, so its own alerts fill the gap.
items.tip: Create a free alert for "translator" and "مترجم".

items.name: Bayt job alerts
items.what: Job site across the Arab region. It also blocks this tool.
items.tip: Create a free alert for translator jobs in Egypt and remote.
